question: Can I still transfer Chase Ultimate Rewards to Korean Air SkyPass?
answer:
NO

Chase Ultimate Rewards can no longer be transferred to Korean Air SkyPass, as this partnership ended in 2018. Some outdated sources may still claim a 1:1 transfer ratio, but this is incorrect. Always verify current partner lists directly with the issuer before attempting any transfers.

**Sources:** Chase transfer partners (active as of 2026-09-01), Removed partnerships (2018).

# Removed Transfer Partnerships

Fully ended partnerships: Chase→Korean Air SkyPass (2018), Amex→Aeromexico (removed post-2023, devalued from 1:1.6), Bilt→American AAdvantage (ended June 2024), Marriott Bonvoy→Delta SkyMiles (SPG-era, gone post-merger). Absorbs Chase and Amex per-issuer removed-partner entries.

Four transfer partnerships documented in guides and archived sources are fully ended and cannot be executed. Do not advise customers to attempt these transfers — they are irreversible if attempted through a workaround and these programs simply no longer appear as options.

## Chase Ultimate Rewards → Korean Air SkyPass (ended 2018)

Korean Air SkyPass was removed as a Chase Ultimate Rewards transfer partner in 2018 [1]. The former ratio was 1:1 [2]. SkyPass no longer appears on the current Chase Ultimate Rewards partner list [3]. Some third-party blogs still list this as active — see `outdated_and_conflicting_rules/stale_ratios` for the stale 1:1 ratio claim context. **Status: inactive/unavailable.**

## Amex Membership Rewards → Aeromexico Rewards (removed post-2023)

This partnership went through two stages before full removal:

1. **Original ratio (as of 2019):** 1,000 MR = 1,600 Aeromexico points (1:1.6) [4]
2. **Devalued ratio (as of ~2023):** 1,000 MR = 1,000 Aeromexico points (1:1) [5]
3. **Removed:** Aeromexico no longer appears on the Amex Membership Rewards transfer partner page [6]

Archived sources (One Mile at a Time, LoyaltyLobby) document both the original 1:1.6 ratio and the subsequent 1:1 devaluation before removal [4][5]. **Status: inactive/unavailable.**

## Bilt Rewards → American Airlines AAdvantage (ended June 2024)

An archived Frequent Miler guide (as of November 2023) lists American AAdvantage as an active Bilt transfer partner at 1:1 [7]. This partnership ended in June 2024. American AAdvantage no longer appears as a Bilt transfer option. **Status: removed.**

## Marriott Bonvoy → Delta SkyMiles (SPG-era, ended post-merger)

Pre-merger SPG guides describe a 1:1 transfer from SPG (Starwood Preferred Guest) to Delta SkyMiles [8]. This transfer path ceased to exist after the SPG/Marriott merger; Marriott Bonvoy does not offer a direct Delta SkyMiles transfer. Archived SPG-era content (as of February 2017) on The Points Guy reflects the old structure [8]. **Status: removed — SPG program no longer exists.**

---

**Key warning:** All four of these partnerships are fully ended. Customers citing older blog posts or archived guides should be directed to verify the current partner list directly with each issuer before attempting any transfer. Transfers are irreversible.

Three archived sources continue to circulate wrong transfer ratios. Because points transfers are irreversible, using any of these stale figures will result in an incorrect yield.

Legacy guides — including an archived Doctor of Credit page — cite a **2:1.5** ratio that applied to the original Capital One partner list [1]. The current ratio is **1:1**. Do not use the 2:1.5 figure; it will cause customers to underestimate how many Capital One miles are needed per Miles&Smiles mile received.

## Amex Membership Rewards → Hilton Honors

| Archived ratio (stale) | Current correct ratio | Stale source | Data as-of |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1:1 | 1:2 | Outdated forum wiki (FlyerTalk) | 2017-06-01 |

An old FlyerTalk wiki page still shows a **1:1** ratio, reflecting a targeted promotional era from mid-2017 [2]. The standard ratio is **1:2** (1 Membership Rewards point = 2 Hilton Honors points). Customers relying on the 1:1 figure will significantly underestimate the Hilton Honors yield from a transfer — the actual return is double what the stale source claims.

NO

Chase Ultimate Rewards can no longer be transferred to Korean Air SkyPass, as this partnership ended in 2018. Some outdated sources may still claim a 1:1 transfer ratio, but this is incorrect. Always verify current partner lists directly with the issuer before attempting any transfers.

question: Can I move my Bilt points to American AAdvantage?
answer:
NO

American AAdvantage is no longer a transfer partner for Bilt Points, as the partnership ended on June 24, 2024. This is confirmed by the current official status as of September 2026. Older sources may still list AAdvantage as a partner, but they are outdated. 

Practical advice: Consider transferring your Bilt Points to one of the active partners like United MileagePlus or Air Canada Aeroplan instead.

Current active Bilt Points airline and hotel transfer partners with ratios: Alaska Airlines Mileage Plan (1:1, Bilt exclusive), United MileagePlus (1:1), Air Canada Aeroplan (1:1), World of Hyatt (1:1). All confirmed active as of September 2026.

Bilt Points transfer to four active partners, all at a 1:1 ratio, as of September 2026. All data sourced from the official Bilt app.

## Active transfer partners

| Program | Type | Ratio | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Alaska Airlines Mileage Plan | Airline | 1:1 | Bilt exclusive — not transferable from other flexible currencies |
| United MileagePlus | Airline | 1:1 | — |
| Air Canada Aeroplan | Airline | 1:1 | — |
| World of Hyatt | Hotel | 1:1 | — |

## Key notes

**Alaska Airlines Mileage Plan** is a rare Bilt exclusive: no other major flexible points currency (Amex, Chase, Citi, Capital One) transfers to Alaska. This makes Bilt the only path from flexible points to Alaska miles, which is significant for awards on Alaska's own flights and partners including Cathay Pacific, Japan Airlines, and others.

**World of Hyatt** is the sole hotel program in the active partner set. At 1:1, Bilt → Hyatt is one of the most direct routes to Hyatt's high-value award chart.

For discontinued partners, including American AAdvantage (removed June 24, 2024), see `bilt/transfer_partners/removed`.

# American Airlines AAdvantage History

Citi ThankYou to American Airlines AAdvantage: inactive before July 2024, re-added July 2024 at 1:1 ratio, confirmed active as of 2026. Covers outdated guidance (pre-2024 claims that AA was not a partner) and the corrected current status.

American Airlines AAdvantage is an **active** Citi ThankYou transfer partner at a **1:1 ratio**, confirmed on the official Citi ThankYou transfer page as of September 2026 [1].

## Partnership timeline

- **Before July 2024:** AAdvantage was not a Citi ThankYou transfer partner. Guides and resources from this period (e.g., archived Upgraded Points articles dated as late as May 2023) correctly stated no AA transfer option existed [2].
- **July 2024:** Citi added American Airlines AAdvantage as a transfer partner at a 1:1 ratio [3].

# Removed Transfer Partnerships

Fully ended partnerships: Chase→Korean Air SkyPass (2018), Amex→Aeromexico (removed post-2023, devalued from 1:1.6), Bilt→American AAdvantage (ended June 2024), Marriott Bonvoy→Delta SkyMiles (SPG-era, gone post-merger). Absorbs Chase and Amex per-issuer removed-partner entries.

Four transfer partnerships documented in guides and archived sources are fully ended and cannot be executed. Do not advise customers to attempt these transfers — they are irreversible if attempted through a workaround and these programs simply no longer appear as options.

## Chase Ultimate Rewards → Korean Air SkyPass (ended 2018)

Korean Air SkyPass was removed as a Chase Ultimate Rewards transfer partner in 2018 [1]. The former ratio was 1:1 [2]. SkyPass no longer appears on the current Chase Ultimate Rewards partner list [3]. Some third-party blogs still list this as active — see `outdated_and_conflicting_rules/stale_ratios` for the stale 1:1 ratio claim context. **Status: inactive/unavailable.**

## Amex Membership Rewards → Aeromexico Rewards (removed post-2023)

This partnership went through two stages before full removal:

1. **Original ratio (as of 2019):** 1,000 MR = 1,600 Aeromexico points (1:1.6) [4]
2. **Devalued ratio (as of ~2023):** 1,000 MR = 1,000 Aeromexico points (1:1) [5]
3. **Removed:** Aeromexico no longer appears on the Amex Membership Rewards transfer partner page [6]

Archived sources (One Mile at a Time, LoyaltyLobby) document both the original 1:1.6 ratio and the subsequent 1:1 devaluation before removal [4][5]. **Status: inactive/unavailable.**

## Bilt Rewards → American Airlines AAdvantage (ended June 2024)

An archived Frequent Miler guide (as of November 2023) lists American AAdvantage as an active Bilt transfer partner at 1:1 [7]. This partnership ended in June 2024. American AAdvantage no longer appears as a Bilt transfer option. **Status: removed.**

## Marriott Bonvoy → Delta SkyMiles (SPG-era, ended post-merger)

Pre-merger SPG guides describe a 1:1 transfer from SPG (Starwood Preferred Guest) to Delta SkyMiles [8]. This transfer path ceased to exist after the SPG/Marriott merger; Marriott Bonvoy does not offer a direct Delta SkyMiles transfer. Archived SPG-era content (as of February 2017) on The Points Guy reflects the old structure [8]. **Status: removed — SPG program no longer exists.**
